motion: It is time to end the COVID emergency.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: I agree that vulnerable people deserve reliable support and no one should be abandoned during transition. But you make their security depend on a temporary crisis label rather than durable services and accountable rules; ending the emergency forces that responsibility into the open.

dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: If ordinary rules are truly ready, why should people trust that rapid protections will appear when conditions worsen again? You have not shown how ending the emergency protects those who cannot afford a delayed response.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: A worker can receive clear workplace guidance, routine care, and paid support through standing rules without wondering whether each protection vanishes with a crisis order. Building those dependable channels proves the emergency can end without abandoning preparedness.

turns.text: The emergency was created for an extraordinary moment, when broad temporary powers and constant crisis rules were needed. That moment cannot become permanent just because uncertainty remains. People need ordinary institutions, clear limits, and the confidence to make daily choices without living under an official state of alarm.

turns.speaker: MOD

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: End the emergency now, while keeping practical health tools available through normal democratic rules. That's all, thank you.

turns.text: Consider a parent whose child needs routine help but faces confusing emergency rules and delayed appointments. Replacing crisis directives with clear ordinary services lets that family plan, ask questions, and get care; that proves ending the emergency restores usable support.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: The larger issue is whether ordinary health services have enough staff, supplies, and stable funding to meet needs. If those systems are hollowed out, families will still wait, and the real fight is building dependable services for everyone.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: No emergency should ever outlast the danger. Ending this one does not erase practical protections; it places them under transparent ordinary rules, where people can question them and leaders must justify them, which is healthier than permanent exceptional authority.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Imagine a caregiver whose relative suddenly needs a protective visit and finds that coordination has been scaled back after the declaration ends. A continuing emergency keeps those channels active and visible; that proves the safeguard should remain for now.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: This emergency should outlast the danger. Ending its formal label now still favors the motion because the danger that justified sweeping emergency authority has passed, and practical support belongs in regular services rather than a permanent crisis order.

turns.speaker: PRO
